title: Totoro Forest
intro: This lesson fades out words as the audio plays. Click a sentence to jump back to that point.
sentences: Totoro Forest is a group of protected forests in the Sayama Hills, an area between Tokyo and Saitama.
This region is widely known as one of the models for the animated film My Neighbor Totoro, and it still preserves the natural environment that inspired Totoro's hometown.
To protect this valuable site, a National Trust project began in 1990.
Through donations from supporters, land has gradually been purchased and protected.
The first forest was created in 1991, and by March 2025, the number of protected forests had increased to 64.
Although each forest is small, together they play a significant role as homes for many plants and animals.
Visitors are asked to stay on walking paths instead of entering the forests.
This procedure helps protect wildlife and reduce potential dangers.
Guided tours and volunteer activities are also available for people who want to learn more and make a contribution to nature protection.
Unlike ordinary forests, Totoro Forest shows how small protected areas can play a significant role in supporting wildlife and environmental learning.
